chunks: Al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A man wakes up in the morning without intending fasting, and when the sun rises, a thought comes to him to fast.' He said: 'If he intends fasting before the sun passes its zenith (zawal), it is counted for him from his day; and if he intends it after the zenith, it is counted for him from the time he intended.'

key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: Solar noon / passing of the zenith
key_terms.قَضَاءُ الصَّوْمِ: Making up a missed fast (implied context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I forget to intend fasting before dawn and decide to fast later in the morning?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of *niyyah* (intention) for voluntary fasting, establishing that the validity of the fast depends on the timing of the intention relative to solar noon (*zawal*). It distinguishes between making the fast valid for the whole day if intended before noon, versus counting only from the moment of intention if made after, reflecting the Shia juristic view that intention can be made during the day for voluntary acts. This ruling underscores the importance of conscious commitment in worship, even when the initial dawn intention is missed.
